digest.component_or_area: MCP error surface and error classification
propositions: MCP tool failures currently surface as unstructured prose or ad-hoc partial shapes (_mcp_reads explain_criterion, _mcp_llm) without a machine error discriminator, forcing agents to pattern-match human text to distinguish ticket_not_found from concurrency_conflict from gate refusal

CLI already emits structured error_envelope(error, input, message, exit_code) via error_envelope() helper with codes like ticket_not_found, concurrency_conflict, claim_failed, but these codes are bare string literals at 12 call sites with no central registry or library-side classifier

The read facade flattens TicketNotFoundError subclasses back to generic RebarError, and RebarError/ConcurrencyError/TrackerRootError set returncode/stderr but not .message, so error_code_for() must classify by isinstance not message substring and use str(exc) not exc.message to avoid AttributeError on concurrency paths

MCP must emit the same vocabulary codes as CLI by introducing error_code_for(exc)->str classifier in _errors.py plus KNOWN_ERROR_CODES frozenset, re-exported as rebar.error_code_for for library consumers and cross-interface test verification

MCP tool guards must catch RebarError/ConcurrencyError/ConcurrencyMismatch/CommandError/LLMError and raise McpEnvelopeError(RuntimeError) carrying .envelope dict (built via error_envelope with code from error_code_for), and the two soft-error returns (_mcp_reads explain_criterion {error,kind}, _mcp_llm {error,...}) must add vocabulary codes while preserving agent-branching fields (kind, resolution_class, retryable, diagnostic)

Schema must relax error_envelope.required from [error, input, message] to [error, message] so target-less MCP failures omit input, CLI envelopes remain unchanged, and tests pin code stability per message rewording via cross-interface agreement (library, CLI, MCP emit identical error for same failure)
